summary: The diff adds new frontend Sign In/Sign Up pages and a client-side session context, and introduces a backend migration that changes order.owner from Principal to ?Principal. However, the requested native username/password auth + backend session-token authorization is not implemented: backend logic still relies on Principal-based access control, frontend auth is simulated via localStorage with insecure password handling, and order ownership/dashboard filtering is not enforced via the new username identity/session token model.

missing_requirements.requirement: Implement a native authentication system (no Google / no Internet Identity) with username/password sign-up and sign-in; passwords never stored/returned in plaintext (store only salted/hashed representation).
missing_requirements.reason: Frontend implements a simulated localStorage-based user DB and base64-encodes passwords; there is no backend signUp/signIn, and no salted/hashed password storage in backend is shown.

missing_requirements.requirement: Add backend session support for username/password authentication and use it to authorize all protected operations using a session token (replace Principal-based authorization checks).
missing_requirements.reason: backend/main.mo still authorizes using Principal caller permissions (AccessControl/hasPermission/isAdmin) and order ownership checks against caller Principal; no signUp/signIn/getSession methods or session-token authorization are shown.

missing_requirements.requirement: Update order ownership/queries so dashboards show only the signed-in user’s orders under the new username/password identity; order detail blocked if not owned unless admin; admin can list/update all orders using admin session.
missing_requirements.reason: Backend order ownership remains tied to Principal (owner : ?Principal and comparisons to caller). Frontend user order filtering is implemented via localStorage order-id lists per username because 'backend doesn't have getUserOrders', and there is no session-token-based enforcement for order detail ownership.

missing_requirements.requirement: Ensure admin login works under the same username/password system with an admin role in the new user account model; frontend AdminGate uses new backend admin check based on session token.
missing_requirements.reason: Admin role is determined purely client-side (localStorage user record; isAdmin when username === 'admin'). Backend admin gating remains Principal/AccessControl-based; no backend session-token admin check is shown.

missing_requirements.requirement: Add a conditional state migration so upgrading from existing Internet Identity/principal-owned data does not break at upgrade time and existing orders remain readable after upgrade.
missing_requirements.reason: A migration file exists and backend references it, but the shown migration only changes Order.owner from Principal to ?Principal and does not demonstrate conditional handling for the broader shift to username/password sessions (nor that existing orders remain readable via admin listing under the new auth model). Given truncation, the required conditional/complete migration for the requested auth/ownership changes is not evidenced.

hallucinated_features.description: Client-side user database and authentication using localStorage (rf_falcon_users) instead of backend-based signup/signin.
hallucinated_features.reason: BuildRequest requires a native username/password auth system with backend handling and hashed/salted passwords; it does not request localStorage-based auth simulation.

hallucinated_features.description: Passwords stored as base64-encoded strings in localStorage (btoa(password)).
hallucinated_features.reason: This is insecure and contradicts the requirement that passwords are never stored/returned in plaintext and must be stored only as salted/hashed representation by the backend; base64 is not hashing.

hallucinated_features.description: Admin role assignment hardcoded as username === 'admin' in the frontend.
hallucinated_features.reason: BuildRequest asks for an admin role concept in the new user account model and backend-admin determination based on session token; it does not specify or request a client-side username-based admin shortcut.

hallucinated_features.description: User order ownership tracking in the frontend via localStorage keys user_orders_<username> because backend lacks getUserOrders.
hallucinated_features.reason: BuildRequest requires order ownership and queries to be updated under the new identity model and enforced (including order detail blocking) using backend authorization; it does not request a client-side localStorage workaround for ownership.
